lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Cameron Pillai is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Cameron is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Thornfield watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer.
d41: 🕯️ Cameron Pillai is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Cameron kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Cameron's gone." Paolo looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Cameron." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Caitlin blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Fine Woodworking (Level 1). Joints that hold without nails: mortise, tenon, and the humble dovetail.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Repair & Mending (Level 1). Look at what's broken before you touch it: find the failure point, not the symptom. Most breaks are one small thing.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Cameron Pillai, 41 days. The mantle passes to Caitlin Peng.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Caitlin Peng, 19 — a carpenter. Their hands know different work now: Green Whisper, Echo Location, Berserker Rage.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Cameron — and Cameron is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.

d41: The fire knew Caitlin before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
